summary: Ran the modular-lifting step at fixed p (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z1013_lift.py, p = 409 and 2521): for y = ρz the surface 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx) is linear in x with coefficient z(4ρz − p(ρ+1)), which is a unit for some unit z modulo every odd modulus, so EVERY unit ratio ρ occurs on the surface mod m (PROVED, one line; checked exactly: 408/408 mod 409, 1008/1008 mod 1009, 2520/2520 mod 2521; mod 2^k unit ratios need 2 | gcd(y,z) since y,z odd is impossible mod 2). Hence 'reconstruct y/z from modular solutions mod m' returns ALL fractions of height ≤ √(m/2): at p = 409 the candidate set has ≈ 5.1·10⁴ (m = p²) and 2.1·10⁷ (m = p³) members against 12 true ratios (recall 0.50 / 1.00, precision 1.2·10⁻⁴ / 5.8·10⁻⁷); at p = 2521, 1.9·10⁶ / 4.9·10⁹ candidates vs 9 true ratios (recall 0.33 / 1.00). The modular data carry no information beyond the height bound already measured in Pass 1 (max H(y/z) ~ p^1.94), so lifting reduces to enumerating all small fractions.
not_done: No CRT-lifting over composite moduli mixing 2-power and odd parts beyond the parity remark; only p = 409, 2521 (the lemma is general).
next: None — a non-vacuous filter would need global (height/archimedean) information, not congruences.

summary: Computed f(n) for ALL n ≤ 3·10⁴ (U = unordered and O = ordered, repo count program, 4 cores ~4 min; agrees with Pass 1's n ≤ 3000 table) and ran the item's test (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z1363_dirichlet.py): F(3)/ζ(3)³ = 0.294944 (U) / 1.263405 (O), stable to 6 digits; F(2)/ζ(2)³ ≈ 1.878 (U) / 10.35 (O) with an explicit log³-tail correction (partial sums 8.127 / 44.69 at N = 3·10⁴, still drifting ~1% per tripling of N). Neither quotient is an Euler product: the coefficients g = f∗μ∗μ∗μ (resp. f∗μ∗μ∗μχ₋₄) have g(1) = f(1) = 0, satisfy g(mn) = g(m)g(n) on only 0.06% (0.10%) of 75 809 coprime pairs (corr 0.01 / 0.67), and g(p) = f(p) grows like log²p (mean g(p)/log²p = 1.14, 1.33, 1.52 on [10², 2·10²), [10³, 2·10³), [10⁴, 2·10⁴)), so F/ζ³ is not 'bounded × Euler product'. BRAINSTORM/anal_dirichlet_series.md discusses D_I, D_II poles (order 4 at s=1, ET Thm 1.7) but not this test; no loop/functional equation suggests itself from the data.
not_done: No analytic continuation attempt; F(2) is an estimate (tail model c·log³n with locally fitted c), not a certified value.
next: None for the Euler-product form; any structure would have to be sought in D_II's shifted-convolution form (anal_dirichlet_series §2).

summary: Ran the N₁(p) census (b = 1 line / López Type A counts, scripts/z29_census.c countlist, exact) over all 969 074 primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 10⁷ plus p ≡ 1 (24) in (10⁷, 10⁸] (all N₁ ≤ 2 cases beyond p = 61 are ≡ 1 (24)): zeros only 193, 2521, 66529; near-failures N₁ ∈ {1,2} number 41, the last two at 2 031 121 and 2 654 401, none in (10⁷, 10⁸]. Residue-matched quantiles (controls p′ ≡ p mod 24, same size, PARI quadclassunit/qfbclassno; scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z0804_quantiles.py): for the 38 targets N₁ ≤ 2, p > 100, mean L(1,χ_p) quantile 0.73 and 61% above 0.8, but mean h(−4p)/√p quantile 0.54 (13% below 0.2, vs 20% expected); in the scale-free lower tail (bottom 0.2% of N₁/log²p per log-bin, 1439 primes ≡ 1 (24) in [10⁵, 10⁸]) 78% have L-quantile > 0.8 vs 25% for random same-class primes, while h-quantile < 0.2 occurs at 9.0% vs 19.2% baseline. So Type-A hardness is L(1,χ_p)-driven (EVIDENCE; matches BM_LVALUE.md §3.3 for R(p)); the small-h(−4p) mechanism suggested by 193 does not recur (193 is a small-p artefact: its matched control set has 132 primes).
not_done: p ≢ 1 (24) in (10⁷, 10⁸] not censused (line is trivially solvable there, López/B1_LINE Prop 1.4, but N₁ = 1–2 there was only checked to 10⁷: none beyond 61). quadclassunit is GRH-conditional.
next: None for the item; the L(1,χ_p) dependence is already the campaign's hardness law.

summary: Literature step: Pomerance–Weingartner, arXiv:2511.16817v2 (the item's own reference) §6 + Table 1 already do the item's step far beyond 10¹⁰: 'By sifting with the seven congruences in [ET, Prop 1.9], with 4 replaced by m, we have verified … the m = 6, 7, 8 cases up to 10¹³ … ', and Table 1 lists for m = 8 (= ES_2, 8/n) the complete exception set n ≤ 10¹³: '1, 2, 3, 11, 17, 131, 241' (7 values). So the k = 2 ladder provably (CERTIFIED by PW's computation) ends at 241 up to 10¹³, confirming Pass 1's exact scan to 10⁸ (6 prime failures, last 241). Table 1 also confirms the item's k = 3 entry (m = 12: 24 exceptions ≤ 10¹², last 12241) and covers m = 9…15 to 10¹²; PW conjecture an exception prime in (m², 2m²) for every m ≥ 20, so the ES_k ladder cannot stabilise as k grows.
not_done: No independent re-run beyond 10⁸ (PW's 10¹³ sieve supersedes the planned 10¹⁰ scan); m = 16…48 ladder beyond Pass 1's 10⁷ not extended.
next: If the ladder matters, adapt PW's seven-congruence sieve to m = 16 (k = 4), whose last known failure is 83449.

summary: Did the cost estimate from the source: Mihnea–Dumitru (arXiv:2509.00128 §2) extended Salez's modular filters by S29 (R8 = 2 101 514 classes mod G8 = 25 878 772 920, survivor density 8.1·10⁻⁵, 140 000 prime filters, GMP) and checked [10¹⁷, 10¹⁸] in 'about 2 weeks with a medium setup'; filter-based verification costs a constant per integer of range, so [10¹⁸, 10²⁰] is ≈ 110× that run (≈ 4 setup-years, i.e. O(10²) core-years; each further prime filter roughly halves it per their S29 remark) — easily within volunteer-computing scale. Own measurement (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_verifykernel.c, naive b = 1-pair filter, 1 core): 19, 22.5, 21.9, 28.7 ns per integer of range at 10⁶, 10¹², 10¹⁵, 10¹⁸, i.e. flat in height; a u128 fixed-cell variant runs 3–4·10⁴ candidates/s from 10¹⁸ to 10³⁶. This replaces Pass 1's estimate (trial division ∝ √p ⇒ 10⁷ CPU-years to 10¹⁸), which used the wrong algorithm; my naive kernel is ~10³× slower per integer than MD's (24× denser survivors, ~3700 pair tests per candidate).
not_done: No contact with PrimeGrid/yoyo@home (outreach); MD's core count is unstated ('medium setup'), so core-years are an order-of-magnitude estimate; kernel misses (~2·10⁻⁸ per integer at 10¹⁸, prime ones) would need an exact fallback that was not implemented.
next: If verification beyond 10¹⁸ is wanted, start from MD's public code (github.com/esc-paper/erdos-straus) plus S31/S37 filters rather than a new kernel.

summary: Wrote and benchmarked the census kernel the item asks for, in its cheapest structured form: per candidate n in the Mordell-hard classes it records the least b = 1 certificate (smallest st with st | n+s+t, 4 | st, B1_LINE.md Lemma 1.1) (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_verifykernel.c): 6.8–10·10⁴ candidates/s/core with flat cost from 10⁶ to 10¹⁸ (data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/Z1789/bench.txt), so a least-certificate census of the ≈ 1.2·10⁹ hard-class primes ≤ 10¹² costs ≈ 4 core-hours plus sieving — not the 400–800 CPU-h of Pass 1 (which assumed √p-growing trial division of 4Cp+1). The real bottleneck is data, not CPU: one 4-byte field per hard-class prime to 10¹² is ≈ 5 GB, so a public dataset must be histograms/records, not per-prime rows; verification itself is already at 10¹⁸ (Mihnea–Dumitru 2025, see Z1789), so a crowd project would only add value beyond ~10¹⁹–10²⁰.
not_done: The 10¹² census itself was not run (no repo place for 5 GB; ~4 core-h is above the per-item cap only marginally — could be run as histograms); no crowd project planned (outreach). Smallest C-form / Type I d / e-slice fields not implemented separately (b = 1 line only).
next: If wanted, run the least-certificate histogram census to 10¹² (~4 core-h) and publish record tables only.

summary: No GPU here, so I ran an explicitly substituted CPU proxy of the item's step: a fixed-cell kernel (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_cellkernel128.c) for the hardest static cell n ≡ 1 (mod 38 798 760) (survivor of all b = 1 pair identities with st | G, Mordell-hard), u128 n, testing b = 1 pairs st ≤ 2·10⁵ via precomputed residues: 3.0–4.0·10⁴ candidates/s/core at 10¹⁸, 10²⁰, 10²⁴, 10³⁰, 10³⁶ (flat), mean 5400–5900 pair tests per candidate, 5–15 misses per 2·10⁴ candidates needing an exact fallback. The cell holds 2.6·10¹⁶ integers below 10²⁴, so even at ~10³× GPU speed-up (~3·10⁷/s/device, Assessment) a targeted search samples ~10⁻⁹ of one cell per device-day — useful only as random sampling, not as an adversarial certificate of anything; it cannot test the low-count-cell hypotheses of DISPROOF_AVENUES beyond what the 10¹⁸ census gives.
not_done: No CUDA port or GPU benchmark (no hardware); e-slice test via factoring (p+e)/4 not used (needs ECM/rho at 10²⁴) — replaced by the equivalent modular pair filter; no exact fallback for misses.
next: Only worth pursuing with a concrete adversarial target cell from a model (e.g. least-QNR / L(1,χ_p) preselection), not uniform cell sampling.

summary: Extended the item's table with the new fast exact U(p) (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_fastU.c, O = 3(T1+T2) ordered, validated against the repo count program on all primes < 3000, 14 primes near 10⁶ and 17 primes up to 1.75·10⁸): exact over all 78 498 primes ≤ 10⁶, then 20 log-spaced windows to 10⁸ with 300/120 random primes each (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z0947_sum.py). Σ_{p≤N} O(p)/(N log²N) = 0.877, 0.803, 0.762, 0.731 (N = 10³, 10⁴, 10⁵, 10⁶; exact, reproducing the item's 0.88/0.80/0.77/0.76/0.75 at 10³…2·10⁵), 0.701 ± 0.010 (10⁷), 0.698 ± 0.015 (10⁸); against N log²N loglog N it keeps falling (0.278 → 0.252 → 0.240), so the data favour the ET lower-bound order N log²N (EVIDENCE). Fit ratio = c + d/log N over 10³…10⁸: c = 0.581, d = 2.06 (quadratic-in-1/log N fit c = 0.568); the window means of O(p)/log³p (1.00, 0.91, 0.84, 0.80, 0.78 per decade 10³…10⁸) are still drifting down, consistent with the same limit ≈ 0.58.
not_done: Above 10⁶ the sum is a stratified-sample estimate (±1.4–2.2% 1σ), not exact; no window beyond 10⁸ (fast U costs ~35 s per prime at 10⁹).
next: None needed; the asymptotic constant is only pinned to ~0.6 ± 0.1 by these ranges.

summary: With the new exact fast U(p) (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_fastU.c; agrees with the repo count program on all 2384 primes Pass 1 had in (10⁶, 8·10⁶], on all primes < 3000 and on 17 primes to 1.75·10⁸) I computed U for ALL 78 498 primes ≤ 10⁶ and for all 18 143 primes in the six Mordell-hard classes mod 840 in (10⁶, 10⁷] (this completes Pass 1's p ≡ 1 (840) run: all 3031). Record lows of U(p)/log²p over 50 < p ≤ 10⁶ are exactly 53, 61, 73, 193, 2521 (0.825, 0.651, 0.380, 0.217, 0.147), as the item says; in the hard classes of (10⁶, 10⁷] the minimum is 0.422 at 3 830 401 (U = 97), so no new record (the restriction is justified: 29 of the 30 smallest U/log³p in [10⁵, 10⁶] lie in those classes). The Type-A/R failures do not become records: U(66529) = 38 (0.308), R-zeros 409…8 813 281 all ≥ 0.27. Since mean U/log²p ≈ 0.13 log p grows, the record list is very likely complete (EVIDENCE); the model-guided search to 4·10⁹ (Z0885) found nothing lower either.
not_done: Non-hard classes in (10⁶, 10⁷] not computed (they never held a low in [10⁵, 10⁶]); beyond 10⁷ only model-guided candidates (see Z0885).

summary: Completed the census at all 20 pseudosquares ≤ 10¹⁰ (A002189; 2641 is a(4), the item's 'L₁₃' label is wrong, as Pass 1 noted): new single-n word counter scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_words1.c (exact, equal to the 10⁸ census binary at 5 test n) gives (R, Uv, I3) = (28, 61, 180), (56, 72, 212), (36, 101, 238), (76, 86, 300) at 175244281, 427733329, 898716289, 2805544681, and fast U gives U = 417 (4.28·10⁸) and 471 (8.99·10⁸). Against class-matched controls (same residue mod 840; 100 nearest non-square n for words, nearest primes for U; scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z0762_pseudosq.py) the 12 PRIME pseudosquares 8089…898716289 have U at percentile 0–0.18 in 10 of 12 cases (median ≈ 0.03; U/log³p 0.026–0.060), i.e. they sit at the bottom of their own Mordell-hard class, while R, Uv, I3 percentiles are unremarkable (R 0.02–0.8, median ≈ 0.25; I3 median ≈ 0.4); R = 0 occurs only at the composites 2641 and 18001, never at a prime pseudosquare (minimum R = 2 at 53881). So pseudosquares are an extreme of the L(1,χ_p)/QR-richness hardness law (BM_LVALUE.md §3.3), not an 'approximate T1' (EVIDENCE): no certificate family vanishes on them.
not_done: Full U(2805544681) (composite 127·859·25717) not finished: the segmented count costs ≈ 2.5·10⁴ CPU-s (measured: 4.5–9 s per 2¹⁸-block of x, 5350 blocks), above the cap; partial: the first block alone gives U ≥ 13 002, far above prime controls (≈ 600) because solutions are inherited from the factors. Word controls for n > 10⁸ are primes only.
next: None for the near-T1 hypothesis; pseudosquares are good stress tests for any L(1,χ_p)-based hardness model.

summary: Searched with the new fast exact U(p) (≈0.4 s at 10⁷, 3.6 s at 10⁸, 33 s at 10⁹): exhaustive over all primes ≤ 10⁶ and all 18 143 Mordell-hard-class primes in (10⁶, 10⁷] (29/30 of the lowest U/log³p in [10⁵,10⁶] lie in these classes), then model-guided — the top hard-class primes by the partial Euler product S(p) = Σ_{q≤400} −log(1−χ_p(q)/q) (Spearman −0.63 with U/log³p on the 1e6–1e7 data): top 1000 of 158 955 in [10⁷,10⁸), 120 of 1.41·10⁶ in [10⁸,10⁹), 24 of 4.35·10⁶ in [10⁹, 4·10⁹], plus 69 pseudosquare-neighbourhood primes to 2.8·10⁹. No prime above 2·10⁵ beats 2521's 0.0187: the smallest values are 0.0233 (471 241, U = 52), 0.0278 (3 830 401), and only 15 primes > 2·10⁵ fall below 0.03, all ≤ 8.7·10⁶; the model-guided minima are 0.0322 (37 793 809), 0.0355 (465 751 729), 0.0373 (3 769 072 129). EVIDENCE that U(p) ≥ 0.0187 log³p holds well beyond 2·10⁵ (exhaustive only to 10⁶ / hard classes to 10⁷).
not_done: No exhaustive search beyond 10⁷ and nothing above 4·10⁹ (fast U uses u64 p², and costs ~5 min/prime near 4·10⁹); the S-proxy caught the 1e6–1e7 minimum at rank 596/18 143 only, so the model-guided minima above 10⁷ are upper bounds on the decade minima.
next: None unless a better hardness predictor than the L(1,χ_p) proxy appears.

summary: Decade minima of U(p)/log³p (p ≡ 1 (4)), fast exact U (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_U3minima.py): [10²,10³) 0.0412 (193), [10³,10⁴) 0.0187 (2521), [10⁴,10⁵) 0.0235 (20521), [10⁵,10⁶) 0.0233 (471 241, U = 52 — corrects Pass 1's 0.0278 at 176 401, which came from incomplete data), all exhaustive; [10⁶,10⁷) 0.0278 (3 830 401, exhaustive over the six Mordell-hard classes; a random all-class sample gives 0.039); [10⁷,10⁸) ≤ 0.0322, [10⁸,10⁹) ≤ 0.0355, [10⁹, 4·10⁹] ≤ 0.0373 (model-guided upper bounds, top-S hard primes). Decade medians fall slowly (0.109, 0.102, 0.099 for all primes; ≈ 0.048 for the top-S samples) while the minima rise from 0.019 to ≈ 0.03, i.e. the safety margin min/median grows from 0.17 to ≈ 0.45–0.75 in the computed range (EVIDENCE).
not_done: Decade minima above 10⁷ are not exhaustive (cost ≈ 0.6·10⁶ core-s per decade at 10⁸ even restricted to hard classes); no decade 10¹⁰ (u64 limit of the fast program).
next: Add the min U/log³p column to any future exhaustive hard-class census.
